okfInfo.title: What is OKF?
okfInfo.short1: OKF (Open Knowledge Format) is an open convention for Markdown collections: plain files with a small, uniform frontmatter header.
okfInfo.short2: Every note Plainva creates carries one field — “type”. The bundle version lives once in the root index.md, and existing files are never changed unasked.
okfInfo.short3: That reliable structure is what databases, filters, templates and index.md navigation build on — and it stays plain Markdown that other tools read.
okfInfo.settingsDesc: In short: type, provenance and review marks, the bundle version and index.md management.

binding.title: An artifact belongs to another workspace
binding.explain: {{kind}}: the file names a different workspace id than this vault. It comes from another encrypted vault or was put into the wrong cloud folder.

pathHash.title: An artifact does not match its file name
pathHash.explain: {{kind}}: the file name carries a checksum that does not match the content. The file was renamed or changed on the way.

signature.title: A signature is invalid
signature.explain: {{kind}}: the signature of the device that wrote the file cannot be confirmed. Either the content was changed, or the device's key is not the expected one.

policyChain.title: A policy that does not continue the accepted one
policyChain.explain: A policy version does not build on the chain this device accepted. It comes from a diverged state and is not adopted.

policyUnaccepted.title: Changes use a policy this device has not accepted yet
policyUnaccepted.explain: {{device}} wrote with policy version {{policy}}; accepted here is {{accepted}}. Usually a newer member or a policy change that has not reached this device yet.
policyUnaccepted.hint: After the next policy refresh this usually resolves itself — “Check again” triggers exactly that refresh. If it stays, check under “Devices” whether {{device}} still belongs to the workspace.

authorNotActive.title: Changes from a device that is no longer active
authorNotActive.explain: {{device}} is no longer listed as an active device in the policy. Its changes are not adopted.
authorNotActive.hint: If the device was removed, this is correct. If it should write again, pair it again under “Devices”.

postRevocation.title: Changes from a device after it was revoked
postRevocation.explain: {{device}} lost access. These changes lie beyond the point an authorized device last witnessed for it — they are not adopted.
postRevocation.hint: This is the normal outcome of a revocation and needs no action. Ignore the group if the revocation was intended. If the device should write again, pair it anew under “Devices”.

capability.title: A change the device was not allowed to make
capability.explain: {{device}} wrote something its role does not permit. The change stays out.
capability.hint: If the device should be allowed, change its role under “People & permissions” and check again.

missingParents.title: Changes whose predecessors are missing
missingParents.explain: These changes build on revisions this device does not know. The predecessors have not arrived yet or are gone from the cloud.
missingParents.hint: Waiting and “Check again” usually suffices — the predecessors come with the next refresh. If they stay missing, a device never uploaded them.

chainGap.title: Changes from one device are waiting: the chain is broken
chainGap.explain: This device expects change no. {{expected}} from {{device}}; the cloud holds no. {{found}}. Whatever is missing or replaced in between blocks everything after it — the group covers {{count}} changes.
chainGap.hint: Usually a second copy of the same device is behind it — a development instance with its own storage, say — or a device that was reconnected and counts from 1 again. Let {{device}} sync once and check again here. If you ignore the group, these changes are lost.

chainBlocked.title: Waiting behind a gap
chainBlocked.explain: This change is fine but stands behind a gap in its device's chain. It is adopted as soon as the gap closes.

payloadMissing.title: The content of a change is missing from the cloud
payloadMissing.explain: The change points at an object that is not in the cloud or was altered. The upload is incomplete or was touched from outside.
payloadMissing.hint: Let the device that wrote the change sync once more; it re-uploads the missing object. Then “Check again”.

envelope.title: An encrypted object does not match its change
envelope.explain: The encrypted envelope names a different workspace, object or revision than the change claims. The pair is not adopted.

rollback.title: A device reports an older state than known
rollback.explain: The pointer of {{device}} in the cloud is behind what this device has already seen. A jump backwards is not adopted — it looks like a cloud that was rolled back.

checkpointMissing.title: A checkpoint is missing from the cloud
checkpointMissing.explain: A device points at a checkpoint that is not in the cloud or was altered.

unreadable.title: A file cannot be read
unreadable.explain: {{kind}}: the file is not a valid Plainva artifact — damaged, truncated or written by a newer app version.
unreadable.hint: If Plainva is newer on another device, update this one. Otherwise export the diagnosis; it helps with the investigation.

unknown.title: A check failed
unknown.hint: Export the diagnosis and check again. If nothing changes, the export helps with the investigation.

whatsNew.title: What's new in Plainva {{version}}
whatsNew.highlight1: A remark hangs on a passage, a region of a picture, a table cell or a database property, and the column beside the note shows what it points at.
whatsNew.highlight2Title: Suggesting is a mode of its own
whatsNew.highlight2: You type in a copy of the note, Plainva shows what went and what is new word by word, and one send becomes a round you can apply or decline in one go.
whatsNew.highlight3Title: Publish a slice of your vault
whatsNew.highlight3: Recipients see only what you release and can write back — the encryption behind it is unreviewed, so nothing confidential yet.
whatsNew.highlight4Title: A vault in a folder you pick yourself
whatsNew.highlight4: On the phone a vault may now live in a folder another app keeps — Syncthing or the Files app, for instance.
whatsNew.highlight5: A confirmed deletion travels to your other devices as an intent instead of arriving there as a missing file and being uploaded again.
whatsNew.highlight6Title: One surface for versions and conflicts
whatsNew.highlight6: The left side is always what the note holds right now, the right side is the other version, and the footer prices the decision in lines.

rules.localOnly: Rules run only while Plainva is open, and only over messages Plainva has fetched. This mailbox offers no server-side rules.
rules.localForNow: Rules currently run only while Plainva is open, and only over messages Plainva has fetched. This mailbox could run them on the server — that comes in one of the next steps.
rules.localMobile: Rules run only while the app was in the foreground, and only over messages Plainva has fetched.
rules.bodyNote: A rule checks the message text. That is not in the overview — it takes effect once you open the message.
rules.publishedPartly_one: Rules stored with the provider; {{count}} stay local because the server cannot express them.
rules.publishedPartly_other: Rules stored with the provider; {{count}} stay local because the server cannot express them.
rules.skippedNote_one: {{count}} rules stay local — the server cannot express them.

rules.sieveHint: Rules stored with the provider also run while Plainva is closed ({{host}}). Until then they only apply here, to messages Plainva has fetched.
rules.scriptForeign: The filter script contains a section Plainva cannot read safely — nothing was changed.
rules.graphHint: Rules stored with the provider also run while Plainva is closed (Microsoft). Plainva only replaces the rules it created itself.

commentNotify.enableHint: Plainva has no server, so a remark is noticed during a sync cycle. On the desktop that is almost at once; the phone notices when you open it.
commentNotify.levelAllHint: Every new remark in this vault.
commentNotify.levelMentionsHint: Only when somebody writes @ and your name.
commentNotify.levelRelevantHint: Mentions, replies in threads you wrote in, remarks on your notes, and verdicts on your suggestions.
commentNotify.preview: Show note and text in the notification
commentNotify.previewHint: Off, a notification only says that something arrived — no name, no note title, no text. A locked vault never previews.
